Cambridge new build: your PDI form matters.

Before you get your keys on a new Ontario home: 1) Your builder leads a floor-by-floor walk-through, called the Pre-Delivery Inspection (PDI). 2) You or a designate must attend, and a designate needs written authority. 3) Every item that's incomplete, damaged or not working is recorded on the PDI form. 4) You sign the PDI form, the official record of the home's condition before you move in. 5) Items not fixed by move-in can be reported on Tarion's Initial, Mid-Year or Year-End Form.

Source: Tarion, Pre-Delivery Inspection and claim forms pages.

caption:
$700K Georgetown home. Hidden closing cost?

Example: a $700,000 home, minimum down payment: 5% x $500,000 = $25,000 plus 10% x $200,000 = $20,000, so $45,000 down and a $655,000 mortgage (93.57% loan-to-value). CMHC premium for the 90.01% to 95% band: 4.00% x $655,000 = $26,200, which may be added to the mortgage ($681,200 total). Ontario's 8% sales tax on the premium: $26,200 x 8% = $2,096, which can't be added to the loan and is paid at closing. Cash for the down payment plus the sales tax: $47,096. 25-year amortization; a 30-year amortization adds a 0.20% surcharge. Not included: land transfer tax, legal fees, adjustments.

Sources: CMHC, Premium information for homeowner and small rental loans, and Purchase pages; Ontario sales tax rate of 8% per Ratehub and Nesto (confirm with your lawyer). Lenders also apply the stress test and debt ratios.

Own in Toronto? April 30 matters.

The City of Toronto reported on Nov 2, 2026 that the 2026 Vacant Home Tax declaration period is open. Council set the 2026 tax at 3% of a property's assessed value (current value assessment). The declaration covers how the home was used from Jan 1 to Dec 31, 2026, and owners can declare online through the City's portal until April 30, 2027. My take: put the date in your calendar, and ask the City or your lawyer if you're unsure how it applies to you.

Source: City of Toronto news release, Nov 2, 2026.
